Investment Topics We attended 1Q26 STA’s analyst meeting on May 18. The overall takeaway from the meeting was slightly positive. Details are as follows: ► Stronger 2H26 natural rubber sales volume in sight. Despite a 14% YoY and 6% QoQ decline in natural rubber sales volume in 1Q26 to 342k tons, management remains confident in achieving its 2026 natural rubber sales volume target of 1.6mn tons, implying 13% YoY growth. Management expects natural rubber sales volume to improve in 2H26, driven by restocking demand from tire manufacturers. The recent spike in natural rubber prices due to Middle East tensions led some tire producers to adopt a wait-and-see approach in March. However, management believes customer inventory levels remain relatively low and understocked. Therefore, natural rubber sales volume is expected to recover as customers gradually resume restocking in 2H26, supported by improved visibility on future rubber prices. ► A year of rubber price recovery expected. Due to lower natural rubber supply, the industry is expected to remain in structural deficit. Management therefore expects the natural rubber price in 2026 to remain at USD1.9-2.0/kg based on fundamentals with limited downside even if crude oil prices decline. Meanwhile, management believes the supply deficit should persist as many farmers continue shifting to palm oil cultivation, which offers higher returns per rai than rubber. ► Operational resilience despite El Niño. Management revised up its natural rubber GPM target to 8-9.5% from 8-9%, reflecting an improving natural rubber outlook. Meanwhile, management believes that despite potential supply pressure from an El Niño event, STA is well positioned to secure raw materials, as the company has already diversified its procurement network across 46 collection points domestically and globally, with plans to expand the network to 60 locations in 2026. ► Raising 2026/27/28 earnings forecasts. We raise our 2026/27/28 earnings forecasts by 28%/6%/6% to Bt2.5bn/Bt2.9bn/Bt3.2bn to reflect 1) a 3% increase in our natural rubber sales volume assumptions to 1.51mn/1.56mn/1.61mn tons; 2) a 4% increase in our natural rubber ASP assumptions to USD2/kg; and 3) an 8% increase in our glove ASP assumptions to USD21.7/21.8/22.1 per 1,000 pieces. Valuation and Recommendation ► Maintain Outperform. We roll forward our valuation base year to mid-2027 with a raised YE2026 target price from Bt14.8 to Bt21.9. Our rating reflects a stronger rubber price outlook and GPM expansion that support a 2026 earnings turnaround. Sri Tran Agro-Industry Pcl.
